package_info.why_malicious: The package contains native code and injected logic that abuses system permissions, communicates with a remote C&C server, and injects code into ad SDKs to perform automated ad fraud (clicker behavior) without user consent. It requests excessive permissions and executes code at device startup, enabling persistent, covert malicious activity.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At device boot and on various system events, the code registers a broadcast receiver that allows the app to execute code persistently and covertly.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Requests BOOT_COMPLETED and other system events not needed for a compass app, enabling persistent background execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate compass app should not need to run at boot or listen to system-level events.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Device management or security apps may use BOOT_COMPLETED legitimately.
key_indicators: Excessive intent filters for system events

execution_context.trigger: device boot or system event (via BaseReceiver)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: BaseReceiver loads native library 'kagu-lib' and calls startTicks, which calls clm from com/google/android/gms/internal/JHandler.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At device boot or system event, the app loads a native library and starts a background process that registers workers for C&C communication and ad SDK injection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading native code and registering background workers is unnecessary for a compass app and is used to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps rarely use native code for background tasks unless for performance-critical features.
key_indicators: Native library loading for background tasks
Obfuscated method calls to internal classes

execution_context.file_location: Injected code in Ad SDK classes (e.g., AdMob, Facebook)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On a timer, the code randomly selects an ad-related activity and launches it in the background, simulating user interaction with ads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Randomly launching ad activities is a clear indicator of click fraud.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should only show ads in response to user actions, not in the background or at random intervals.
key_indicators: Random selection of ad SDK classes

execution_context.file_location: Injected into Ad SDK onCreate method

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When an ad activity is created, the code calls a method to simulate a click event on the ad using reflection and MotionEvent.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting code to simulate ad clicks is a hallmark of clicker malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Ad SDKs should not be manipulated to generate fake clicks.
key_indicators: Method call to simulate clicks in onCreate
Use of reflection to invoke click logic

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code programmatically generates MotionEvent objects to simulate user clicks on ads, sending them via reflection to the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Programmatic generation of MotionEvent for ad clicks is a direct method of ad fraud.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: User input should come from real user interaction, not synthetic events.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Periodically, the code contacts a hardcoded C&C server, sending device and app information to retrieve new configuration or commands.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited communication with a remote server for configuration is a strong indicator of C&C activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should not contact unknown servers for hidden configuration.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of app and device data

attack_chain.action: App is installed and requests excessive permissions, including BOOT_COMPLETED.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistence and background execution on device boot.

attack_chain.action: On boot or system event, BaseReceiver loads native code and starts background workers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Background workers for C&C communication and ad SDK injection.

attack_chain.action: Background worker contacts C&C server for configuration and processes commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Receives instructions for ad fraud and click simulation.

attack_chain.action: Injected code launches ad activities at random intervals.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ad activities are created in the background.

attack_chain.action: Injected code in ad activity onCreate simulates user clicks using MotionEvent.
attack_chain.leads_to: Automated ad click fraud, generating revenue for attackers.

behavioral_signatures: App requests BOOT_COMPLETED and other system-level broadcast permissions without clear justification.
Native library loading for background tasks in non-performance-critical apps.
Random or periodic launching of ad SDK activities in the background.
Reflection-based creation and dispatch of MotionEvent objects to simulate user input.
Unsolicited communication with hardcoded C&C servers for configuration.
file_indicators: Presence of native libraries (e.g., kagu-lib) in non-native apps.
Injected or modified Ad SDK classes (e.g., AdmobAdView, FacebookAdInternal).
Excessive or suspicious intent filters in AndroidManifest.xml.
network_indicators: HTTP requests to /api_v5/facebook_api.php or similar endpoints.
Frequent background network activity not tied to user actions.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps that request BOOT_COMPLETED and other system events without clear need, load native libraries for background tasks, or inject code into ad SDKs. Detect reflection-based MotionEvent creation and unsolicited network connections to known C&C infrastructure. Flag apps that launch ad activities in the background or simulate user input programmatically.
